chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Safwan ibn Yahya from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): From a man who walked between As-Safa and Al-Marwah eight paces, what is upon him? He said:
"If it was by mistake, he discards one and counts seven."

key_terms.أَشْوَاطٍ: Paces or cycles (specifically referring to the seven rounds of Sa'i)
key_terms.الصَّفَا: As-Safa (one of the two hills between which pilgrims walk)
key_terms.وَالْمَرْوَةِ: Al-Marwah (the second hill in the Sa'i ritual)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim makes a mistake during the Sa'i between Safa and Marwah?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the fiqh of Sa'i, establishing that an unintentional error does not invalidate the ritual but merely requires discarding the mistaken cycle. This ruling underscores the Shia principle of ease (*rukhas*) in worship, distinguishing between deliberate omission and accidental mistake. It serves as a foundational precedent for the permissibility of partial validity in ritual acts when performed with sincere intent.
